title: Why do American school buses stop with flashing red lights?
sources: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration School Bus Safety

lines.text: Why does every single car on both sides of the road have to come to a complete stop for a school bus?
lines.caps: Why do all cars *stop | for yellow *school buses?

lines.text: In the United States, passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights carries felony-level fines.
lines.caps: Passing a stopped bus brings *massive | fines and *points

lines.text: American school buses feature a dual amber and red lighting system invented in the late nineteen-fifties.
lines.caps: Features a dual *amber | and red warning *system

lines.text: Amber lights flash to warn motorists that the bus is slowing down to drop off children.
lines.caps: Amber lights warn that the *bus | is about to *stop

lines.text: When the bus stops, the driver deploys a mechanical Stop-sign arm and flashes bright red lights.
lines.caps: Red lights flash and a *mechanical | stop sign *extends!

lines.text: This creates an enforced pedestrian safety zone around the vehicle because children often run across blind traffic.
School buses are legally the safest form of passenger transportation in the entire country.
lines.caps: The safest passenger *transport | in the entire *country!
